scenes.tts: If raising Track A is not enough, what else must N G F change?
scenes.caption: If raising TrkA is not enough, what else must NGF change?
scenes.visual: Title card: Only Both Loops Split Them. The frozen 52 to 48 pie.
scenes.narration: If raising TrkA is not enough, what else must NGF change?

scenes.tts: N G F also controls how long its own signal lasts.
scenes.caption: NGF also controls how long its own signal lasts.
scenes.visual: A signal timer appears beside each neuron.
scenes.narration: NGF also controls how long its own signal lasts.

scenes.tts: N G F is caught at the axon tip, far from the cell body. Yet it changes which genes the nucleus turns on.
scenes.caption: NGF is caught at the axon tip, far from the cell body. Yet it changes which genes the nucleus turns on.
scenes.visual: A long axon: NGF binds at the tip in the target; the nucleus sits far away in the ganglion.
scenes.narration: NGF is caught at the axon tip, far from the cell body. Yet it changes which genes the nucleus turns on.

scenes.tts: So the signal has to travel back up the axon. Much of it travels inside endosomes.
scenes.visual: An endosome carrying NGF and TrkA travels up the axon toward the cell body.
scenes.narration: So the signal has to travel back up the axon. Much of it travels inside endosomes.

scenes.tts: One protein that N G F induces, Coronin one, keeps these signaling endosomes active longer.
scenes.caption: One protein that NGF induces, Coronin-1, keeps these signaling endosomes active longer.
scenes.visual: The endosome's timer runs longer when a Coronin-1 tag is attached.
scenes.narration: One protein that NGF induces, Coronin-1, keeps these signaling endosomes active longer.

scenes.tts: It is required for normal competition in the mouse. It is one mechanism, and there may be others.
scenes.visual: Label: Coronin-1, one mechanism. A faint question mark: others?
scenes.narration: It is required for normal competition in the mouse. It is one mechanism, and there may be others.

scenes.tts: Now test the idea in a model. The computational neuroscientists Stefan Mihalas and Ernst Niebur joined the group.
scenes.visual: On screen: Mihalas and Niebur. Equations sketched faintly behind a row of model neurons.
scenes.narration: Now test the idea in a model. The computational neuroscientists Stefan Mihalas and Ernst Niebur joined the group.

scenes.tts: They simulated neurons competing for N G F that the target makes at a constant rate.
scenes.caption: They simulated neurons competing for NGF that the target makes at a constant rate.
scenes.visual: A target releases NGF at a steady rate to a row of model neurons.
scenes.narration: They simulated neurons competing for NGF that the target makes at a constant rate.

scenes.tts: They compared four conditions. No feedback. Feedback on Track A level alone.
scenes.caption: They compared four conditions. No feedback. Feedback on TrkA level alone.
scenes.visual: A grid of four panels; the first two are labelled no feedback and level only.
scenes.narration: They compared four conditions. No feedback. Feedback on TrkA level alone.

scenes.tts: Feedback on signal duration alone. And feedback on both.
scenes.visual: The last two panels are labelled duration only and both.
scenes.narration: Feedback on signal duration alone. And feedback on both.

scenes.tts: Which of the four conditions split the neurons into winners and losers?
scenes.visual: On screen: which panels split? Pause and predict.
scenes.narration: Which of the four conditions split the neurons into winners and losers?

scenes.tts: Only feedback on both. With either one alone, competition failed.
scenes.visual: Only the fourth panel splits into a winning and a losing group. The other three stay bunched.
scenes.narration: Only feedback on both. With either one alone, competition failed.

scenes.tts: The two-neuron arithmetic gives a reason for both failures, at least in a toy version.
scenes.visual: The two-neuron pie returns beside the four panels.
scenes.narration: The two-neuron arithmetic gives a reason for both failures, at least in a toy version.

scenes.tts: Level alone, with capture in proportion to receptor, keeps every ratio fixed. Duration alone never changes the catch, so the shares stay put.
scenes.visual: Pie frozen at 52 to 48 under level only, and frozen again under duration only.
scenes.narration: Level alone, with capture in proportion to receptor, keeps every ratio fixed. Duration alone never changes the catch, so the shares stay put.

scenes.tts: Level and duration together close a loop. A signal that rises faster than the lead feeds the next catch, so in this toy the lead grows.
scenes.visual: Pie climbs toward A under both. Label: the loop closes.
scenes.narration: Level and duration together close a loop. A signal that rises faster than the lead feeds the next catch, so in this toy the lead grows.

scenes.tts: This toy reason is not the published equations. It only illustrates why one loop was not enough.
scenes.visual: Label: toy reason, not the published equations.
scenes.narration: This toy reason is not the published equations. It only illustrates why one loop was not enough.

scenes.tts: In the published simulations, the two loops together separated winners from losers.
scenes.visual: A card: published simulations, two loops together separated winners from losers.
scenes.narration: In the published simulations, the two loops together separated winners from losers.

scenes.tts: The lab described the sequence as four stages.
scenes.visual: Four boxes in a row, empty.
scenes.narration: The lab described the sequence as four stages.

scenes.tts: Naive. A young neuron responds poorly to N G F.
scenes.caption: Naive. A young neuron responds poorly to NGF.
scenes.visual: Box 1 fills: naive, poor response to NGF.
scenes.narration: Naive. A young neuron responds poorly to NGF.

scenes.tts: Sensitization. It gets enough N G F to cross a threshold. From then on, N G F makes it more sensitive to N G F.
scenes.caption: Sensitization. It gets enough NGF to cross a threshold. From then on, NGF makes it more sensitive to NGF.
scenes.visual: Box 2 fills: sensitization, crosses a threshold and becomes more sensitive to NGF.
scenes.narration: Sensitization. It gets enough NGF to cross a threshold. From then on, NGF makes it more sensitive to NGF.

scenes.tts: Competitive advantage. It raises Track A and strengthens the signaling downstream of it.
scenes.caption: Competitive advantage. It raises TrkA and strengthens the signaling downstream of it.
scenes.visual: Box 3 fills: competitive advantage, more TrkA and stronger downstream signaling.
scenes.narration: Competitive advantage. It raises TrkA and strengthens the signaling downstream of it.

scenes.tts: Selection. It wins the supply, and neighbours that stayed behind lose.
scenes.visual: Box 4 fills: selection. Neighbours that stayed behind fade.
scenes.narration: Selection. It wins the supply, and neighbours that stayed behind lose.

scenes.tts: One more piece speeds the split. The next chapter asks how winners treat the losers.
scenes.visual: The losing group dims; a strong neuron turns toward a weak one.
scenes.narration: One more piece speeds the split. The next chapter asks how winners treat the losers.

scenes.tts: Takeaway. N G F raises both receptor level and signal duration. In the published model, only the two together split the neurons.
scenes.caption: Takeaway. NGF raises both receptor level and signal duration. In the published model, only the two together split the neurons.
scenes.visual: End card: published model, level plus duration splits winners from losers.
scenes.narration: Takeaway. NGF raises both receptor level and signal duration. In the published model, only the two together split the neurons.
